/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 20 October 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2593 (47)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3522 (157)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2247 (-39)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1868 (0)
Baltic Handysize Index: 1017 (1)
CAPESIZE
The market continued to gain traction today, with improving sentiment across both the Pacific and Atlantic lifting the BCI 182 5TC by $1,427 to $31,945. The C5 index increased by $0.555 to $13.00, while C3 gained $1.180 to $31.90. In the Pacific, momentum from yesterday’s push carried through into today’s trading, with C5 offers firmly in the $13s against operator bids around $12.50 at the start of the day. Although only one miner was active, operator demand remained healthy, with a premium being paid for earlier ETAs. By later in the day, the sole miner was reported to have fixed at around $12.85, despite many offers continuing to hold in the $13s. The Atlantic also showed signs of improvement, following a handful of fixtures reported by yesterday’s close, with rates in the high $31s achieved on index dates. Today, offers were heard in the low $32s against bids around $31.50, while end-November dates continued to command a premium, with bids around $33.00 to the low $33s. However, the North Atlantic remained a softer pocket, with brokers pointing to a growing tonnage list and limited demand, tempering the broader improvement in sentiment.
PANAMAX
Brokers reported a quieter day in the Atlantic, with limited fixing activity and sentiment remaining under pressure. While some market sources suggested trans-Atlantic fundamentals may be moving towards a more balanced position, as a modest uptick in demand coincides with a less abundant tonnage list, the fronthaul market continued to weaken. Softening demand was said to be prompting owners to revise their rate expectations downward, particularly on US Gulf to China business. EC South America was also described as heavily oversupplied, with a lack of meaningful fronthaul bids forcing owners to further reduce offers in an effort to stimulate chartering interest. The Guo Yuan 26 (75,855 2012) fixed an EC South America trans-Atlantic trip with redelivery Skaw-Gibraltar range at around $33,000 to Bunge. In the Pacific, market participants described a steadier day, with sentiment remaining comparatively more positive. Australian demand was said to be healthy, with some sources suggesting the prompt tonnage list has started to tighten, supporting current fixing levels. By contrast, the North Pacific was viewed as more subdued, with limited fresh enquiry reported, while Indonesia was largely described as balanced in terms of cargo demand and vessel availability. Fixture activity included the Star Explorer (82,362 2024), which reportedly fixed a North Pacific round trip at around $21,000-$22,500 daily, with the scrubber benefit retained by owners. Overall, the P5TC declined by a further $350 to $20,223.
SUPRAMAX
The market appeared to be on a slow start this week, with a softer Atlantic being offset by the firmness in Asia. The North American market declined as the US Gulf and US East coast both remained subdued, with Owners forced to revise their rates to find cover, and the south Atlantic also seemed quieter after a clear out of fronthaul stems last week. The Macka (63,562 2016) Tema 24-26 October fixed a trip via Owendo to China at around $25,500. The strength on the Continent appears to be mainly driven by Russian stems now, with scrap rates receding from recent highs, and the Mediterranean only appeared stronger for the more challenging trades. In Asia sentiment remains bullish, although South East Asia looked flat, whilst backhaul strength seemed very destination driven. There was talk of a 64,000-dwt open South China first half November being fixed for 3 to 5 months redelivery worldwide at $22,500, which looked slightly light compared to the newbuilding GLBS Thalia (64,000 2024) Busan end October which was reported fixed for minimum 4 to about 6 months at $24,250 with Oldendorff Carriers.
HANDYSIZE
The market showed a mixed tone today, with the 7TC average rising slightly by $25 to close at $18,305. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, only minor changes were observed, and the market appeared balanced with rates hovering around last-done levels in most loading areas. The South Atlantic remained finely balanced supported by continued improvement in cargo flows and a shortage of prompt tonnage. In the US Gulf, sources reported further easing in bid and offer levels as charterers and owners gradually adjusted their expectations lower. Meanwhile the Pacific market saw limited activity, although tonnage remained tight and the cargo book healthy. On the period side, a large Handysize vessel was heard fixed for four to six months with delivery in South Brazil and worldwide redelivery in the low $20,000s, although further details were not disclosed.

Atlantic
A 39,000-dwt was heard fixed for a trip delivery Santos redelivery ARAG at $32,000, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
The Ken Sei (31,771 2010) open Singapore on 20 October was fixed for multiple legs at $15,250, although further details were not disclosed.

Market Fundamentals
BHP Q3 Results
In the quarter ending September 2026, BHP announced iron ore production at Western Australian Iron Ore (WAIO) reached 71.9 Mt, marking a 2.4% increase on the year. According to BHP’s report, the company achieved record first quarter (FY27 Jul-Jun) volumes at both its mine and port, despite significant planned maintenance. Total BHP share of WAIO sales stood 3.9 Mt higher year-on-year at 66.3 Mt in the quarter. Total production guidance remained unchanged at 260-272 Mt for FY27. In Samarco, production rose 4.1% year-on-year to 2.2 Mt (50% basis) while sales declined 4.9% to 1.9 Mt during the period.

Anglo American Q3 Results
In its Q3 26 production report, Anglo American reported a 3.8% year-on-year drop in iron ore output to 13.8 Mt. The decline came as production in Kumba fell 18.9% year-on-year to 7.5 Mt, though Minas-Rio production rose 23.6% from the same time last year to 6.3 Mt. The drop at Kumba was primarily driven by a planned DMS plant shutdown in Sishen. Meanwhile, total sales grew 9.3% year-on-year to 15.8 Mt, with Kumba sales up 3.3% to 9.7 Mt.
